_source.file: Master of the Seven Seas — Fleet Roster
_source.note: Sean's combat update. The sheet now carries four things: the roster, a Ratings & Pricing system that prices every hull, the LOCKED combat specification, and a Combat Derived Stats table of per-ship hit chances and average volleys. The combat rules here supersede the '7 Seas — Naval Combat System' document of the same morning. Change this file by re-reading the sheet, not by hand.

supersedes.file: Master of the Seven Seas — Fleet Roster

_notes.note: The blocking item is dissolved rather than answered. The locked rules open with *'There is no ship-level Firepower stat. Every individual cannon makes its own attack using the rules for its gun type.'* So the three gun columns ARE the combat inputs, Speed stays a category rather than becoming 1-10, and the conversion everything downstream was waiting on is cancelled.

_notes.about: Armor and First Strike are back
_notes.note: Both were removed on the morning of 18 September and both return in this specification: armor as a flat subtraction with per-gun-type penetration, First Strike as the Long Gun phase resolving before Light and Heavy. Armor is also rescaled to 0-30 from the old 0-110.
Still the R5 Confederate siege ship. Jessup's legend hull was renamed the Adamant on 18 September so this name could stand; the collision is resolved and nothing here needs to change for it.

_notes.about: Urskin Goliath, and the name URW
_notes.note: Renamed by hand on 19 September at Sean's word: *'Change its name to Urskin Goliath. I am gonna invest a new ship called the Urskin Whaler.'* The Gigantic 1,800-hull dreadnaught is the Goliath; a new, much smaller Urskin Whaler is going into the sheet and is not here yet. The Ship ID moved with the name, CFS-URW-R7-01 -> CFS-URG-R7-01, so that URW is free for the hull that is actually a whaler. That part is a call made here rather than read off the sheet - if the sheet says otherwise on the next import, the sheet wins.

purpose.Purpose: Authoritative working roster for ship progression, economics, ratings, and combat inputs. Ratings & Pricing governs purchase value; Combat Rules and Combat Stats govern the ship-versus-ship simulation model.
purpose.Roster structure: Each faction has four starting ships and eight research unlocks. Research order establishes progression, not strict replacement: efficient, specialized, and logistical ships may remain useful throughout the campaign.
purpose.Faction contrast: The Crown favors standardized progression, disciplined combined fleets, and dominant capital ships. The Confederacy favors asymmetric specialists, retrofits, raiders, living-coral vessels, and military-strategic hybrids.
purpose.Balance philosophy: Every ship needs a clear reason to build it and an intentional weakness. Ships are not required to offer equal value: value monsters, fair-rate designs, specialist overpays, and prestige capitals are all valid when deliberate.
purpose.Pricing system: The Ratings & Pricing tab is the authoritative pricing method. Ship Roster columns T:Z calculate capability points, reference cost, synergy and weakness modifiers, price ratio, and S/A/B/C/D/F purchase-value rating.
purpose.Rating scope: The letter rating measures purchase value only. Build time and maintenance are evaluated separately because they control production tempo and sustainable fleet size.
purpose.Current status: Ship identities and pricing are approved working designs. Combat damage, armor penetration, phase order, accuracy, targeting, retreat, and simulation standards are now locked in the Combat Rules tab. The executable 5,000-trial engine is the next build step; special infrastructure/component damage remains outside the initial model.

armorClasses._note: Armor has four gameplay classes: None, Light, Medium and Heavy. Heavy+ (26-29) and Maximum (30) are pricing sub-bands inside Heavy, used to value elite capital protection without adding new gameplay classes.

capabilityPoints._why: High-tier concentration is more valuable than the same number of scattered low-tier abilities. Escalating weights price threshold effects and capital-ship slot efficiency.

Mobile firepower.when: Fast or Very Fast with at least one T3+ gun battery.

Pursuit hunter.when: Fast or Very Fast with T2+ Long Guns.

Regenerative defense.when: Above-rate Repair with T2+ Armor or Hull.

Independent raider.when: Fast or Very Fast with both Troops and Bombardment.

Combined-arms battery.when: T2+ Long, Heavy, and Light Guns.

Broad utility.when: At least four meaningful T2+ capabilities, including Fast speed or above-rate Repair.

Slow without reach.when: Slow speed and no Long Guns.

Unscreened heavy hull.when: T3+ Armor or Hull with no Light Guns.

Poor recovery.when: Below-rate Repair on a ship with T3+ Armor or Hull.

weaknesses._note: A zero stat alone is not a discount because it already contributes zero points.

buildTimeBands.benchmark: On Rate = 1 build day per gold of actual build cost

maintenanceBands.benchmark: On Rate = ceil(1% of actual build cost) gold per day

combatRules._status: LOCKED. Authoritative combat specification for ship-versus-ship and fleet simulation.
combatRules.principle: There is no ship-level Firepower stat. Every individual cannon makes its own attack using the rules for its gun type.
combatRules.battleTarget: Evenly matched battles should usually resolve in 1-3 player-visible Combat Exchanges.

cannon.attackGranularity: One attack per individual cannon. Ten guns create ten separate attacks.
cannon.hitRoll: Roll d100 for every cannon; the attack hits when the roll is at or below final hit chance after the gun-type modifier.
cannon.example: Armor 25 stops a 25-damage Light hit. A 26-damage Light hit deals 1. A 26-damage Heavy hit faces 13 effective armor and deals 13.

phases.attackCommand: The player chooses Attack/Fight. Snapshot each side's current total Hull, then resolve consecutive internal combat rounds until either side has lost at least 30% of that starting snapshot or a fleet is destroyed.
phases.phaseRule: Target assignment occurs before dice are rolled within each phase.
phases.phase1: Assess every surviving Long Gun and assign targets using the optimal targeting algorithm. Long Guns resolve before Light and Heavy Guns. Roll all assigned Long Gun attacks, then apply all Long Gun damage simultaneously. Ships sunk by Long Guns are removed before Phase 2 and do not fire Light or Heavy Guns.
phases.phase2: Assign every surviving Light and Heavy Gun target as one combined simultaneous firing solution. Light and Heavy Guns on both sides fire before any Phase 2 damage removes ships. Roll all assigned attacks, then apply all Phase 2 damage simultaneously. After the complete round, test the 30% Combat Exchange stop condition.
phases.repair: No repair occurs during combat rounds.
phases.persistence: Damage remains after the round and after the battle until repaired outside combat.
phases.mutualDestruction: Record the analytical result as mutual destruction. In the player-facing UI, loss of the player's entire fleet displays Defeat.

accuracy.formula: CLAMP(75 + gun base modifier + gun-vs-Size modifier + gun-vs-Speed modifier, 10, 95)
accuracy.intent: Heavy accuracy is contextual: average against intended large targets, poor against small/fast targets.
accuracy._note: The Size and Speed read are the TARGET's. These gun-specific matrices replace the former universal Size and Speed modifiers.

targeting.timing: Assign targets before rolling attacks. Long Guns optimize separately in Phase 1; Light and Heavy Guns optimize together in Phase 2.
targeting.expectedDamage: For each gun/target pair: Hit Chance x expected post-armor damage.
targeting.expectedShotsToKill: CEILING(Remaining Hull / Expected Damage per shot); an attack that cannot penetrate receives no viable-kill score.
targeting.targetThreat: Estimate the target's next-volley weapon output from its surviving individual cannons.
targeting.priorityScore: Target Threat / Expected Shots to Kill
targeting.allocation: Assign the next cannon to the viable target with the highest priority score. Track expected assigned damage and stop assigning to that target once an expected kill is covered; then recalculate.
targeting.overkillControl: This spreads fire when further shots would be expected overkill.
targeting.noncombatTransports: Transports with zero guns remain valid targets but are considered only after armed targets are handled.
targeting.tieBreaking: Break equal priority scores randomly to prevent perfectly repetitive battles.
targeting.visibility: The targeting math is internal and is not a visible ship stat.

retreat.volley: Every surviving enemy Long Gun receives one attack when the opposing fleet flees.
retreat.targeting: Use the same optimizer; target hit chance naturally accounts for Speed and Size.
retreat.damage: Use normal Long Gun damage (2d20), 50% armor penetration, and the Long Gun +-0 accuracy modifier.
retreat.resolution: Apply the retreat volley simultaneously; surviving fleeing ships then escape.
retreat.success: Flee never fails and never forces an additional normal round.
retreat.noLongGuns: If the pursuing fleet has no surviving Long Guns, the fleeing fleet takes no retreat attacks.

simulation.coverage: Every ship versus every ship, including mirrors; Swift versus Swift is N/A.
recorded: average internal rounds and Combat Exchanges
simulation.targetDuration: Evenly matched battles should usually resolve in 1-3 player-visible Combat Exchanges; one Exchange may contain multiple internal combat rounds.
simulation.randomness: Each cannon rolls its own d100 hit roll and its own damage dice.
simulation.openBoundary: Special infrastructure or component damage has not yet been defined in the roster and is excluded from the initial simulator.

designRules.Early-game power: Starting ships may be strong, but multiple high-tier capabilities require major drawbacks such as poor efficiency, fragility, Slow speed, weak repair, narrow specialization, or production constraints.
designRules.Fleet structure: Each faction fields four starting ships followed by eight research unlocks. Research should expand fleet-building choices rather than make every earlier hull obsolete.
designRules.Crown doctrine: Standardized combined-arms fleets, dependable progression, strong Heavy Guns and capital ships, and deliberate reliance on escorts to cover specialist weaknesses.
designRules.Confederacy doctrine: Asymmetric specialists, fast raiders, retrofits, amphibious reef technology, regeneration, and ships that trade standardization for unusual strategic advantages.
designRules.Weapon system: Each cannon attacks separately. Light Guns are accurate 2d20 weapons with no penetration; Long Guns are lower-accuracy 2d20 weapons with 50% penetration and first strike; Heavy Guns are the least accurate 4d20 weapons with 50% penetration.
designRules.Long Guns: A midgame technology milestone. Long Guns fire in the first-strike phase and receive one free retreat volley against a fleeing fleet.
designRules.Bombardment: A strategic siege rating used against fortifications and locations. It never contributes to ship-to-ship damage; specialized ordnance may justify Bombardment without naval Heavy or Long Guns.
designRules.Value philosophy: Ships are not expected to offer equal general value. S-tier value monsters and deliberately inefficient specialists are allowed, but every extreme needs a clear strategic purpose and visible counterweight.
designRules.Pricing authority: Ratings & Pricing defines the authoritative reference-price process. Ship Roster columns T:Z apply it automatically to every ship.
designRules.Three economic levers: Purchase cost, build time, and maintenance are separate. A ship should rarely dominate all three without explicit approval and simulation priority.
designRules.Endgame: Majestic remains the strongest individual ship and the only Maximum Armor 30 hull. Urskin Goliath keeps the greatest hull and Heavy Gun mass; Coral-Class supplies Heavy Armor 29, regeneration, and combined arms. One of either Confederate capital loses to Majestic, while two of either—or one of each—should defeat it reliably.

ships.Design Notes: No Armor; 300 Hull; 2 Light Guns. A medium exploration transport whose modest threat helps preserve its four embarked troops.
No Armor; 90 Hull; 4 Light Guns. Very Fast and cheap enough to swarm, but deliberately fragile.
Heavy Armor 24; 650 Hull; 8 Heavy and 6 Light Guns. Powerful but Slow, poorly repairing, costly to maintain, and intentionally D-tier.
Heavy Armor 25; 900 Hull; 7 Heavy and 4 Light Guns. A starting capital assault ship with high upkeep and an escort dependency; intentionally D-tier.
Medium Armor 18; 500 Hull; 4 Heavy and 7 Light Guns. An efficient general-purpose upgrade over Morningstar.
Light Armor 8; 250 Hull; 1 Heavy and 5 Light Guns. Fast multirole workhorse with rapid construction and intentionally inefficient upkeep; A-tier.
Heavy Armor 25; 700 Hull; 4 Long and 4 Heavy Guns. Durable fleet anchor with no Light Guns and weak repair.
Heavy Armor 24; 700 Hull; 7 Heavy and 9 Light Guns. Advanced, durable value warship with exceptional repair.
Medium Armor 14; 150 Hull; 5 Long and 10 Light Guns. Elite Very Fast pursuit interceptor; S-tier value offset by extreme maintenance and a fragile hull.
Heavy Armor 22; 400 Hull; 7 Long, 8 Heavy, and 9 Light Guns. Broad offensive backbone with no troop role.
Heavy Armor 28; 1,200 Hull; 6 Long, 14 Heavy, and 3 Light Guns. Mobile assault super-capital with troop capacity and an escort dependency.
Maximum Armor 30; 1,600 Hull; 10 Long, 16 Heavy, and 10 Light Guns. Strongest individual ship; enormous cost, build time, and upkeep constrain it.
No Armor; 70 Hull; no guns. Very Fast exploration craft priced at B-tier strategic value; never used in Swift mirror combat.
No Armor; 250 Hull; 2 Light Guns. Fast retrofit transport with two troop capacity; C-tier purchase value.
Medium Armor 18; 350 Hull; 1 Heavy and 2 Light Guns. Slow improvised defender with poor repair; C-tier.
Light Armor 6; 300 Hull; 5 Light Guns. Regenerating early defender whose value is sustained operations, not armor penetration.
No Armor; 140 Hull; 1 Heavy and 6 Light Guns. Fast raider with troops and bombardment; deliberate S-tier value monster.
Light Armor 7; 120 Hull; 2 Heavy and 5 Light Guns. Compact conventional fleet warship with no strategic payload.
Medium Armor 18; 175 Hull; 4 Long, 1 Heavy, and 2 Light Guns. Fast armored assault ship with troops and bombardment.
Heavy Armor 24; 350 Hull; 7 Heavy and 4 Light Guns. Capital hunter with strong repair and troop capacity but no Long Guns.
Heavy Armor 25; 750 Hull; 8 Long and 1 Heavy Gun. Slow siege specialist with no Light Guns and poor repair.
Light Armor 5; 250 Hull; 12 Light Guns. Fast apex anti-small combatant with narrow specialization.
Heavy Armor 25; 1,800 Hull; 7 Long and 13 Heavy Guns. Largest hull and invasion platform; one loses to Majestic, while a pair reliably wins.
Heavy Armor 29; 1,100 Hull; 7 Long, 8 Heavy, and 9 Light Guns. Regenerating combined-arms capital; one loses to Majestic, while a pair reliably wins.
